title: Football Australia calls for government to reverse World Cup screening ban in Melbourne
content:
Football Australia has criticised the decision for World Cup matches to not be screened at Melbourne’s Federation Square, and called for it to be reversed.

Katrina Sedgwick, CEO and director of Melbourne Arts Precinct, which governs Federation Square, said on Wednesday that Australia’s matches at this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada, and Mexico would not be screened at the venue due to the behaviour of a “small number of people” which was “simply unacceptable and damaging to Fed Square”.

Australia’s football governing body responded by saying it was “extremely disappointed” by the decision and urged the Victorian Government and the Melbourne Arts Precinct to reverse it, arguing “World Cups are moments when fans unite to celebrate and create lasting memories”.

“Football Australia has spoken with the Victorian Government and the Melbourne Arts Precinct, expressing its strong disappointment and requesting that they overturn this decision,” a statement read.

The venue has hosted live watch parties for Australia supporters since 2006, and videos of fans celebrating went viral at the last World Cup in 2022 as the nation reached the knockout stage of the tournament for the first time in 16 years. However, there were incidents of supporters being injured by flares, other projectiles and crowding, per Australian reports.

A year later, for the women’s World Cup, the screening of Australia’s third-placed play-off match was cancelled after fans stormed the barricades of the venue during the semi-final against England. In quotes reported by ABC, acting Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police Wendy Steendam criticised “very disappointing” behaviour by a “small few”.

However, Football Australia CEO Martin Kugeler has called on supporters to urge the Victorian Government and Melbourne Arts Precinct to “correct” the “disappointing” decision to not screen matches “in the best interests of football fans, local businesses and all Victorians”.

“The FIFA World Cup is the biggest sporting event in the world and unites Australia’s multicultural communities, while reinforcing our national identity,” Kugeler said.

“Live sites create iconic moments for Australian sports fans. They bring all Australians together to celebrate and cheer our National Teams competing on the biggest stage.

“Melbourne is one of Australia’s sporting and multicultural capitals, and this decision goes against this tradition.

“Federation Square has created some of the most memorable moments in Australian sporting history, dating back to the Socceroos’ historic 2006 FIFA World Cup matches and the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup.”

Australia face Turkey (June 14), co-hosts United States (June 19) and Paraguay (June 26) in Group D of this summer’s World Cup.
